title: Chapter 66
content:
The suffocating humidity weighed on Il-hyun as he crossed the grounds. Glancing toward the second floor of the villa, a light was still glowing in Jakyeong’s suite.

Still awake?

Keeping his distance and restricting himself to polite, superficial greetings for two full days was driving him out of his mind. He was dying to see that sharp, indignant scowl again—the way the kid bristled at every dirty joke.

A dozen times a day, a primal urge clawed at his throat, demanding he spread those firm, high thighs and bury himself to the hilt.

Endure it.

He bit down hard on his cigarette filter, forcing the hunger back into the dark. Yet no matter how many cigarettes he burned through, the desire refused to dwindle; tonight, it burned hotter than ever.

Fuck it. This isn't working.

If he set foot in that house right now, he knew he’d march straight up the stairs and pin Lee Ja-kyeong to the mattress.

Needing something cold to shock his system, he kicked off his designer loafers, shed his jacket, unlooped his silk tie, and strode directly into the pool. Submerging his body in the water was the only way to cool the fever in his blood.

A night guard patrolling with a shepherd cast a wary glance his way, but Il-hyun waved him off with a flick of his wrist. Releasing all tension from his limbs, he surrendered his weight to the water, floating face-up beneath the dark sky.

His ears dipped below the surface, drowning out the ambient hum of the world into absolute, echoing silence. It felt remarkably peaceful.

A few stray raindrops began kissing his exposed face. Suspended in the water, it felt almost like retreating back into the dark sanctuary of his mother's womb.

Long before his birth, when his mother first realized she was carrying a second child, she had spiraled into pure, unadulterated madness. In her eyes, the fetus clawing for life in her belly was nothing more than a demon. She had pounded her abdomen with closed fists, hurled herself down flights of concrete stairs, and secretly ingested black-market abortifacients.

Yet by some twisted, unyielding tenacity, he had survived it all, forcing his way into the light of day.

Chairman Kang had rejoiced over the birth of another son, but throughout Il-hyun’s childhood, his mother's eyes held only boundless, venomous hatred. As a young boy, starved for maternal warmth, he had engaged in increasingly bizarre, macabre antics just to earn a single glance—unwittingly driving her further into revulsion. There were days when he had genuinely believed the fault was his own: that an aberration who never should have existed had mistakenly slipped into the world.

He was far past such pathetic self-pity now. Since he had survived, he wanted everything. He wanted to claim the absolute summit, to grind this entire rotten world beneath the heel of his boot. And to achieve that, he needed unassailable, absolute power.

He closed his eyes, letting the quiet wash over him as rain splattered against his cheeks.

Then, a sudden, concussive splash ruptured the silence.

Il-hyun’s eyes snapped open. He planted his feet on the bottom of the basin, surfacing in a spray of water.

Standing before him in the waist-deep pool, drenched to the bone, was Lee Ja-kyeong.

The boy had abandoned the safety of the house, wading straight into the deluge to seize Il-hyun's arm in a desperate, white-knuckled grip. Beneath the wet fringe plastered across his forehead, those wide, dark eyes held a faint, unmistakable flicker of panic.

"Why are you looking at me with that face?"

"What face?" Jakyeong snapped defensively.

The response was sullen and sharp, but Il-hyun’s instincts registered the truth instantly: the kid had dove into the storm out of pure, genuine fear for his life.

Curving his palm overhead, Il-hyun formed a makeshift shield against the driving rain, using his other thumb to tenderly wipe the streaming water from Jakyeong’s brow. Normally, the boy would have swatted his touch away with venomous disgust.

Tonight, he stood completely still.

Ah. Now I see.

Now I finally understand the kind of creature you are.

"Let's get out of the rain," Il-hyun said softly, his fingers closing gently around the boy's wrist. "You'll catch a cold."

He led Jakyeong up the steps of the shallow end. Outside, the downpour had intensified into a blinding torrent.

They stepped into the quiet foyer, grabbing towels from the entrance console to bludgeon the worst of the moisture from their clothes. Without a word, Jakyeong headed up the grand staircase, while Il-hyun turned toward his own suite on the ground floor.

After a hot shower, Jakyeong pulled on fresh loungewear, briskly rubbing a dry towel through his hair. As if on cue, the violent deluge outside tapered off, dying into absolute stillness.

Looking out the bedroom window, the pool below sat vacant and glassy beneath the ambient lights, devoid of any trace of what had just transpired. It felt surreal—almost as if he had been bewitched by an apparition.

Why on earth did I jump in there?

Cursing himself for the foolish lapse in judgment, he sank onto the edge of the mattress.

Knock, knock.

The door eased open, revealing Kang Il-hyun holding a steaming porcelain mug.

"May I come in?"

Jakyeong gave a curt nod, and Il-hyun stepped inside, setting the tea on the nightstand before taking the armchair opposite the bed.

Fresh from the shower, he wore a loose charcoal robe. With his damp, dark hair falling naturally across his forehead rather than slicked back into an immaculate corporate comb, he looked strikingly young—almost disarmingly gentle.

"Thank you for earlier."

"For what?"

"To be honest... I was in a rather dark place tonight," Il-hyun confessed, staring down at his hands. "You might have heard from the staff... but today marks the anniversary of my mother's death."

"..."

"I had this foolish thought that if I floated there in the dark, I might catch a glimpse of her face. But instead... you appeared."

A faint, self-deprecating smile pulled at the corner of Il-hyun's lips.

Jakyeong sat in stunned silence. Was he genuinely grieving?

He had written the man off as a soulless, bloodthirsty sociopath—a monster devoid of human warmth. It was hard to process the vulnerability sitting right in front of him. Then again, hadn't Il-hyun brought up his dead mother before when fishing for sympathy?

Il-hyun bit his lower lip, averting his gaze as he rubbed his palms over his face. When he looked up, the rims of his dark eyes were subtly, delicately flushed with red.

Jakyeong’s stomach twisted with unease. What is this? Why is he acting like this?

The man sitting before him seemed entirely stripped of his usual fangs.

Holding Jakyeong's gaze with a soft, mournful focus, Il-hyun broke the quiet.

"Ja-kyeong... I have a favor to ask."

"What is it...?"

"Would you let me sleep here tonight?"

"..."

"I have no ulterior motives. I'm just... frightened of being alone tonight. To be honest, around this time of year, I'm plagued by horrific nightmares. Not that you'd ever believe me, of course."

I definitely don't. If anything, Kang Il-hyun was the architect of other people's nightmares.

Yet the man didn't push or wheedle. He simply kept his head lowered, long dark lashes fluttering against his cheekbones as he stared at his folded hands.

"I'd... rather you didn't," Jakyeong answered, keeping his voice firm.

At the flat refusal, Il-hyun’s heavy lids lifted. The crimson tinge in his eyes had deepened.

Jakyeong felt his throat lock up. Il-hyun offered a fractured, bittersweet smile that looked genuinely heartbreaking.

"My apologies. That was an unreasonable request."

Without another word of complaint, Il-hyun rose to his feet, offered a quiet wish for a good night's rest, and turned toward the door.

Jakyeong bit his lower lip. There's no reason on earth I should be comforting this bastard.

Yet an old memory flared unbidden in his chest.

After fleeing to China as a ten-year-old child, Jakyeong had spent years trapped in the grip of night terrors—dreaming of his dead parents clawing their way out of rusted oil drums, shrieking like vengeful ghouls that he should have died with them. On those nights, Wang Han would sit beside his cot, gently patting his back until dawn broke. Even now, the nightmare occasionally resurfaced, waking him in a cold, suffocating sweat.

"On the edge..."

Jakyeong’s voice cut through the quiet, freezing Il-hyun on the threshold.

"You can stay. But keep your distance... and don't try anything funny."

As Il-hyun turned around, the faintest twitch of a smile seemed to grace his lips for a fraction of a second. Jakyeong eyed him with sudden suspicion, but the sheer, crushing melancholy etched across Il-hyun's face made it impossible to accuse him of theatrics. Surely he isn't the kind of degenerate who would use his own dead mother as bait for a cheap trick... right?

Il-hyun slipped under the duvet, lying flat on his back.

The atmosphere in the king-sized bed was suffocatingly awkward. Jakyeong rolled onto his side, putting his back to the man. Much better.

He closed his eyes, willing himself to drift off, when a solid radiating warmth pressed flush against his spine.

I knew it.

Jakyeong spun around to glare, only to find Il-hyun’s forehead buried deeply into the nape of his neck. The towering, broad-shouldered corporate predator was curled tightly against him like an abandoned, shivering stray.

The visual struck an unsettlingly familiar chord.

"Just let me borrow your back for tonight," Il-hyun murmured, his voice heavy with a melancholic rasp. His sharp jaw locked tightly several times, as if fighting back a swell of unshed tears.

Jakyeong let out a quiet sigh, entirely resigning himself to the situation.

Il-hyun’s left arm slid over Jakyeong’s waist, loosely pulling him close. True to his word, he went no further. He simply lay there, his deep, rhythmic breathing occasionally hitched with a quiet, heavy sigh.

Then, a rigid, scorching mass pressed firmly against the curve of Jakyeong’s buttocks.

Jakyeong’s entire frame locked into stone.

Scowling, he tried to slide forward, but Il-hyun’s grip on his waist held him securely in place. Jakyeong shifted his hips again, only for the hard length to track him with relentless precision, nudging insistently against his rear.

Losing his patience, Jakyeong pried the heavy arm off and rolled over to face him. At point-blank range, their breaths mingled in the dark.

"Excuse me, Director Kang."

"President."

"Right... President Kang. If you're wallowing in such profound grief, why the hell is your cock rock-hard?"

"Do you stop eating or using the restroom when you're sad?" Il-hyun replied smoothly.

"..."

"It's purely physiological. Completely detached from my emotional state... so pay it no mind."

Delivered with such deadpan, sorrowful gravity, calling it out as pure bullshit felt absurdly difficult. To make matters worse, with his bangs damp and falling over his eyes, the man looked infuriatingly innocent.

While Jakyeong was busy cursing him internally, Il-hyun leaned his forehead down, burying his face directly into the center of Jakyeong’s chest.

It happened so fast Jakyeong had no time to shove him away. Though he was wearing a thin t-shirt, the heavy bridge of Il-hyun's nose pressed through the cotton, his warm breath seeping directly onto bare skin. Jakyeong pushed at the broad shoulders, but the man didn't budge an inch. Worse still, Il-hyun's stubbled cheek kept grazing deliberately over the sensitive bud of his nipple.

"Wait a second. Hold on—"

"Don't push me away..." Il-hyun whispered, his voice trembling with manufactured fragility. "I just need to be comforted."

"..."

Left with no room to maneuver, Jakyeong went still. Il-hyun tightened his arms around the boy's frame, letting his heavy lids drift shut. Instead of his sharp, tailored cologne, his skin carried the fresh, sweet fragrance of white peaches from the bath. He felt like an entirely different person—so much so that it was almost disorienting.

"Good night," Il-hyun murmured, his tone dripping with delicate sorrow.

Preoccupied with the strange, quiet warmth in his chest, Jakyeong never noticed the corners of Kang Il-hyun’s lips slowly, victoriously curving into a wicked, predatory smirk.
